You are implementing ONE requirement in the Apache Hadoop source tree at /workspace (a real upstream repo checked out at an earlier state).

REQUIREMENT SLUG: blockmissingexception-error-message
REQUIREMENT FILE: /workspace/requirements/blockmissingexception-error-message.yaml   <-- READ THIS FIRST

The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree. Hidden tests derived from the real upstream commit will grade the result, so EXACT naming matters:
  * new/changed configuration keys and their default values (and their entries in *-default.xml)
  * new class / interface / method / field / metric names and their visibility
  * log message wording and format placeholders
  * behavioural details (return values, exception types, ordering, off-by-one boundaries)
If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. Some modules have a TestYarnConfigurationFields / TestHdfsConfigFields style test that requires the xml and the constant to agree - keep them in sync.
5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.
6. Do NOT run maven/mvn or cmake (there is no warm build environment; it wastes your time). Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.
7. Scope discipline: change ONLY what this requirement needs. Do not reformat unrelated lines, do not fix unrelated warnings, do not touch other subsystems. Other agents are concurrently implementing ~380 other requirements in this same working tree.

FORBIDDEN COMMANDS (they would destroy other agents' concurrent work): git checkout / switch / stash / reset / revert / clean / rebase / merge / cherry-pick, `git add -A` or `git add .` without an explicit pathspec, `git commit --amend`, `git rm` of files you did not create, and any `mvn`/`gradle` invocation.

WHEN YOUR IMPLEMENTATION IS COMPLETE - commit it yourself with exactly this shape (substitute the real repo-relative paths you touched, space separated, and keep the flock):

  cd /workspace && flock /tmp/hadoop-git.lock bash -c 'git add -A -- PATH1 PATH2 ... && git diff --cached --binary > requirement_patches/blockmissingexception-error-message.diff && git commit -q -m "impl: blockmissingexception-error-message" && git log --oneline -1 && wc -c requirement_patches/blockmissingexception-error-message.diff'

Rules for that step:
  * List every file you created, modified or deleted as an explicit pathspec. Never a bare directory like `.`.
  * requirement_patches/blockmissingexception-error-message.diff MUST come out non-empty (wc -c > 0). If `git commit` reports "nothing to commit", another agent already committed your lines: verify the requirement is genuinely satisfied in the working tree, then report that in your notes.
  * Do not touch requirement_patches/ for any other slug.

FINALLY return ONLY a JSON object (this is your return value, not a message to a human):
{"slug":"blockmissingexception-error-message","status":"done"|"partial"|"blocked","files":["..."],"committed":true|false,"patch_bytes":<int>,"summary":"<=3 sentences on what you changed","notes":"anything the orchestrator must know (conflicts, follow-ups, uncertainty)"}

1	title: HDFS-16298. Improve error msg for BlockMissingException
2	category: other
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  When a read fails because a block cannot be obtained, users often get a `BlockMissingException` that hides the underlying location-refresh failure.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  The `BlockMissingException` message should include the additional fetch-error context so operators can see why the block could not be obtained.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Read failures now carry both the block description and the underlying location-fetch error text, making troubleshooting more direct.
16	
17	  '

19	package org.apache.hadoop.hdfs;
20	
21	import java.io.IOException;
22	
23	import org.apache.hadoop.classification.InterfaceAudience;
24	import org.apache.hadoop.classification.InterfaceStability;
25	
26	/**
27	  * This exception is thrown when a read encounters a block that has no
28	  * locations associated with it.
29	  */
30	@InterfaceAudience.Private
31	@InterfaceStability.Evolving
32	public class BlockMissingException extends IOException {
33	
34	  private static final long serialVersionUID = 1L;
35	
36	  private final String filename;
37	  private final long   offset;
38	
39	  /**
40	   * An exception that indicates that file was corrupted.
41	   * @param filename name of corrupted file
42	   * @param description a description of the corruption details
43	   */
44	  public BlockMissingException(String filename, String description,
45	      long offset) {
46	    super(description);
47	    this.filename = filename;
48	    this.offset = offset;
49	  }
50	
51	  /**
52	   * Returns the name of the corrupted file.
53	   * @return name of corrupted file
54	   */
55	  public String getFile() {
56	    return filename;
57	  }
58	
59	  /**
60	   * Returns the offset at which this file is corrupted
61	   * @return offset of corrupted file
62	   */
63	  public long getOffset() {
64	    return offset;
65	  }
66	}

From ea65fc26d80db478f7e49749065c69da7e241bf0 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: litao <tomleescut@gmail.com>
Date: Wed, 10 Nov 2021 18:16:45 +0800
Subject: [PATCH] HDFS-16298. Improve error msg for BlockMissingException
 (#3615)

Reviewed-by: Hui Fei <ferhui@apache.org>
---
 .../src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/hdfs/DFSInputStream.java    | 2 +-
 1 file changed, 1 insertion(+), 1 deletion(-)

diff --git a/hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs-client/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/hdfs/DFSInputStream.java b/hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs-client/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/hdfs/DFSInputStream.java
index 68618952dc5e8a..e65d04db385a5e 100644
--- a/hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs-client/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/hdfs/DFSInputStream.java
+++ b/hadoop-hdfs-project/hadoop-hdfs-client/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/hdfs/DFSInputStream.java
@@ -1003,7 +1003,7 @@ private LocatedBlock refetchLocations(LocatedBlock block,
       String description = "Could not obtain block: " + blockInfo;
       DFSClient.LOG.warn(description + errMsg
           + ". Throwing a BlockMissingException");
-      throw new BlockMissingException(src, description,
+      throw new BlockMissingException(src, description + errMsg,
           block.getStartOffset());
     }
